hook.text: Cross two inbred corn lines and the offspring outperforms both parents. Farmers call it hybrid vigor.

buildup.text: Inbreeding weakens plants over generations. But crossing two inbred lines produces an explosive burst of growth.

discovery.text: Hybrid corn yields jumped 20–30% over open-pollinated varieties. The US adopted hybrids almost completely by 1960.

twist.text: Farmers can't save hybrid seeds—offspring lose vigor. They must buy new seed every year from companies.

climax.text: This dependence on purchased seed industrialized agriculture and reshaped the seed business forever.

punchline.text: Better seeds, but only if you buy them every season.

quiz.question: Why can't farmers save and replant hybrid seeds?
options: Offspring lose hybrid vigor and underperform
